结果已经明确了一半：

CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL：当前 Kconfig 整段缺失，upstream 有完整配置，因此 .config 无法生成该值。
sys_startup_fn()：两个 esp_start.c 完全相同；但当前版本缺少 upstream 中声明该函数的 esp_start.h，所以出现隐式声明。

还需确认 Kconfig 插入位置，以及 upstream 如何包含 esp_start.h。执行下面的只读命令：

cd ~/openvela-work/contest284/nuttx

echo "=== 当前 Kconfig 330-430 ==="
sed -n '330,430p' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

echo "=== upstream Kconfig 330-430 ==="
sed -n '330,430p' \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

echo "=== Kconfig 局部差异 ==="
diff -u \
  <(sed -n '320,440p' arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig) \
  <(sed -n '320,440p' ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig) \
  | sed -n '1,260p'

echo "=== esp_start.c 文件头 ==="
sed -n '20,70p' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.c

echo "=== upstream esp_start.c 文件头 ==="
sed -n '20,70p' \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.c

echo "=== esp_start.h 是否存在 ==="
ls -l \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h \
  2>&1

echo "=== 谁包含 esp_start.h ==="
grep -Rns --include='*.c' --include='*.h' --include='Make.defs' \
  'esp_start.h' \
  arch/risc-v/src \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src 2>/dev/null \
  | sed -n '1,100p'

暂时不要直接在 .config 里写：

CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL=0

因为它会在重新配置时丢失。正确做法应是恢复 upstream 的 Kconfig 配置块，让 olddefconfig 自动生成；sys_startup_fn() 也优先恢复 upstream 的正式头文件声明，而不是随手在 .c 中增加声明。

文档
思考了 25s

现在可以确认：

esp_start.c 已正确包含 esp_start.h。
当前 esp_start.h 是旧版本，缺少 sys_startup_fn() 声明。
CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL 整个配置块确实没有进入当前 Kconfig。
当前和 upstream 的 Kconfig 排列差异很大，不能直接按 upstream 行号复制，否则可能再次破坏菜单结构。

再做最后一次只读定位：

cd ~/openvela-work/contest284/nuttx

echo "=== esp_start.h 完整差异 ==="
diff -u \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h \
  | sed -n '1,240p'

echo "=== 当前 Kconfig 菜单结构及关键配置 ==="
grep -nE \
  '^menu |^endmenu|^config ESPRESSIF_(SIMPLE_BOOT|BOOTLOADER|CPU_FREQ|MAX_CPU_FREQ|MIN_CPU_FREQ|LOG_LEVEL)' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig \
  | sed -n '1,260p'

echo "=== upstream Kconfig 菜单结构及关键配置 ==="
grep -nE \
  '^menu |^endmenu|^config ESPRESSIF_(SIMPLE_BOOT|BOOTLOADER|CPU_FREQ|MAX_CPU_FREQ|MIN_CPU_FREQ|LOG_LEVEL)' \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig \
  | sed -n '1,260p'

echo "=== 当前 SIMPLE_BOOT 附近 ==="
grep -n -B15 -A30 \
  '^config ESPRESSIF_SIMPLE_BOOT' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

echo "=== 当前第一个外设配置前后 ==="
grep -n -B12 -A12 \
  '^config ESPRESSIF_TWAI0' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

完成这一步后，修复应当是：

从 upstream 精确移植 esp_start.h 中缺少的函数声明；
将官方 Espressif Log Level 配置块插入当前 Kconfig 的正确菜单边界；
执行 make olddefconfig，由 Kconfig 自动生成 CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL=0；
再清理编译。

不会直接硬编码 .config，也不会整份覆盖当前 openvela 的 Kconfig。

粘贴的文本 (1)(20260809-051756).txt
文档
思考了 1m 9s

现在证据充分，可以做两个精确移植：

esp_start.h 与 upstream 只有 SPDX 和 sys_startup_fn() 声明不同，因此可直接同步该头文件。
Log Level 配置块应插在当前 Bootloader and Image Configuration 菜单之前，位置与 upstream 一致。

先同步头文件：

cd ~/openvela-work/contest284/nuttx

cp \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/esp_start.h

再提取并插入 upstream 的官方 Log Level 配置块：

P4_LOG_BLOCK=/tmp/esp32p4_log_level.kconfig

sed -n \
  '/^menu "Espressif Log Level"$/,/^endmenu # Espressif Log Level$/p' \
  ~/openvela-work/upstream/nuttx/arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig \
  > "$P4_LOG_BLOCK"

wc -l "$P4_LOG_BLOCK"

P4_BOOT_LINE=$(grep -n \
  '^menu "Bootloader and Image Configuration"$' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig \
  | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)

echo "Bootloader menu line: $P4_BOOT_LINE"

sed -i \
  "$((P4_BOOT_LINE - 1))r $P4_LOG_BLOCK" \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

确认没有重复插入：

grep -c '^menu "Espressif Log Level"$' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

grep -c '^config ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL$' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

grep -n -B3 -A5 '^config ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL$' \
  arch/risc-v/src/common/espressif/Kconfig

git diff --check

前两个计数都必须为 1。

然后让 Kconfig 自动生成配置：

make olddefconfig

验证：

grep -E \
  '^CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL(_NONE)?=' \
  .config

grep -E \
  '^#define CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL(_NONE)? ' \
  include/nuttx/config.h

L0 无调试日志配置下，预计得到：

CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL_NONE=y
CONFIG_ESPRESSIF_LOG_LEVEL=0

最后重新构建：

make clean

make -j2 2>&1 \
  | tee ~/openvela-work/logs/contest284_esp32p4_build11.log

接下来如何验证最小NCS

按上下文，“NCS”应为 **NSH**。

当前状态：

- `build24` 已成功，`nuttx.bin` 镜像校验有效。
- 还不能判定 L0 通过，因为当前环境没有 `/dev/ttyACM*` 或 `/dev/ttyUSB*`，尚未完成实板启动。
- 官方标准是：烧录后串口出现 `NuttShell (NSH)` 和 `nsh>`，才算 L0 成功。[最小 NSH 基线](https://github.com/open-vela/docs/blob/dev-ai-contest-2026/zh-cn/contest_2026/hardware_porting/defconfig_reference/minimum_nsh_baseline.md)

**实板验证**

1. 连接端口：
   - 烧录口：`/dev/ttyACM0`
   - UART0 控制台：`/dev/ttyUSB0`
   - 波特率：115200
   - UART 引脚：GPIO37 TX、GPIO38 RX

2. 先打开控制台：

```bash
picocom -b 115200 /dev/ttyUSB0
```

3. 另开终端烧录：

```bash
cd ~/openvela-work/contest284/nuttx
source ~/venvs/esp-tools/bin/activate

make flash \
  ESPTOOL_PORT=/dev/ttyACM0 \
  ESPTOOL_BINDIR=./
```

若无法进入下载模式，按住 `BOOT`，点按 `RESET`，再释放 `BOOT`。

4. 看到 `nsh>` 后依次运行：

```text
help
uname -a
ps
free
uptime
sleep 1
uptime
```

5. 通过条件：
   - UART 收发正常。
   - `help`、`uname`、`ps`、`free` 返回正常。
   - 两次 `uptime` 持续增长，验证 SYSTIMER/IRQ/tick。
   - `sleep 1` 能返回提示符。
   - 冷启动三次均能进入 `nsh>`，无 panic、异常或重复复位。

当前 defconfig 仍有 `FS_PROCFS`、`TESTING_GETPRIME`、`TESTING_OSTEST` 三项非最小内容；最终提交前应只删除这三项并重建，不扩展网络、文件系统或其他外设。

      Kconfig option is explicitly checked during startup to ensure proper
      configuration. This validation prevents runtime issues from configuration
      mismatches.

   137	    };
   138	
   139	  systimer_hal_set_tick_rate_ops(&systimer_hal, &ops);
   140	  systimer_ll_set_counter_value(systimer_hal.dev,
   141	                                SYSTIMER_COUNTER_OS_TICK,
   142	                                0);
   143	  systimer_ll_apply_counter_value(systimer_hal.dev,
   144	                                  SYSTIMER_COUNTER_OS_TICK);
   145	  systimer_hal_counter_can_stall_by_cpu(&systimer_hal,

   147	                                        false);

   149	  systimer_hal_connect_alarm_counter(&systimer_hal,
   150	                                     SYSTIMER_ALARM_OS_TICK_CORE0,

   156	                                 SYSTIMER_ALARM_OS_TICK_CORE0,

   161	  systimer_hal_enable_alarm_int(&systimer_hal,

    62	int group_setupidlefiles(void)
    63	{
    64	  int ret = OK;
    65	#if defined(CONFIG_DEV_CONSOLE) || defined(CONFIG_DEV_NULL)
    66	  int fd;
    67	#endif
    68	
    69	  sched_trace_begin();
    70	
    71	  /* Open stdin, dup to get stdout and stderr. This should always
    72	   * be the first file opened and, hence, should always get file
    73	   * descriptor 0.
    74	   */
    75	
    76	#if defined(CONFIG_DEV_CONSOLE) || defined(CONFIG_DEV_NULL)
    77	#  ifdef CONFIG_DEV_CONSOLE
    78	  fd = nx_open("/dev/console", O_RDWR);
    79	#  else
    80	  fd = nx_open("/dev/null", O_RDWR);
    81	#  endif
    82	  if (fd == 0)
    83	    {
    84	      /* Successfully opened stdin (fd == 0) */
    85	
    86	      nx_dup2(0, 1);
    87	      nx_dup2(0, 2);
    88	    }
    89	  else
    90	    {
    91	      /* We failed to open stdin OR for some reason, we opened
    92	       * it and got some file descriptor other than 0.
    93	       */
    94	
    95	      if (fd > 0)
    96	        {
    97	          sinfo("Open stdin fd: %d\n", fd);
    98	          nx_close(fd);
    99	        }
   100	      else
   101	        {
   102	          serr("ERROR: Failed to open stdin: %d\n", fd);
   103	        }
   104	
   105	      sched_trace_end();
   106	      ret = -ENFILE;
   107	    }

   109	  /* This configuration can confuse user programs and libraries.
   110	   * Eg. a program which opens a file and then prints something to
   111	   * STDERR_FILENO (2) can end up with something undesirable if the
   112	   * file descriptor for the file happens to be 2.

   108	      write(OUTFD(pstate), g_nshgreeting, strlen(g_nshgreeting));
   109	
   110	#ifdef CONFIG_NSH_MOTD
   111	#  ifdef CONFIG_NSH_PLATFORM_MOTD
   112	      /* Output the platform message of the day */
   113	
   114	      platform_motd(vtbl->iobuffer, IOBUFFERSIZE);
   115	      dprintf(OUTFD(pstate), "%s\n", vtbl->iobuffer);
   116	#  else
   117	      /* Output the fixed message of the day */
   118	
   119	      dprintf(OUTFD(pstate), "%s\n", g_nshmotd);
   120	#  endif
   121	#endif
   122	
   123	      /* Execute the login script */
   124	
   125	#ifdef CONFIG_NSH_ROMFSRC
   126	      nsh_loginscript(vtbl);
   127	#endif
   128	    }
   129	
   130	  /* Process the command line option */
   131	
   132	  if (argc > 1)
   133	    {
   134	      if (strcmp(argv[1], "-h") == 0)
   135	        {
   136	          nsh_output(vtbl, "Usage: %s [<script-path>|-c <command>]\n",
   137	                     argv[0]);
   138	          return EXIT_SUCCESS;
   139	        }
   140	      else if (strcmp(argv[1], "-c") == 0)
   141	        {
   142	          /* Process the inline command */
   143	
   144	          if (argc > 2)
   145	            {
   146	              return nsh_parse(vtbl, argv[2]);
   147	            }
   148	          else
   149	            {
   150	              nsh_error(vtbl, g_fmtargrequired, argv[0]);
   151	              return EXIT_FAILURE;
   152	            }
   153	        }
   154	      else if (argv[1][0] == '-')
   155	        {
   156	          /* Unknown option */
   157	
   158	          nsh_error(vtbl, g_fmtsyntax, argv[0]);
   159	          return EXIT_FAILURE;
   160	        }
   161	      else
   162	        {
   163	#ifndef CONFIG_NSH_DISABLESCRIPT
   164	          /* Execute the shell script */
   165	
   166	          return nsh_script(vtbl, argv[0], argv[1], true);
   167	#else
   168	          return EXIT_FAILURE;
   169	#endif
   170	        }
   171	    }
   172	
   173	#ifdef CONFIG_NSH_DISABLE_ECHOBACK
   174	  /* Disable echoback */
   175	
   176	  if (isatty(INFD(pstate)))
   177	    {
   178	      struct termios cfg;
   179	
   180	      if (tcgetattr(INFD(pstate), &cfg) == 0)
   181	        {
   182	          cfg.c_lflag &= ~ECHO;
   183	          tcsetattr(INFD(pstate), TCSANOW, &cfg);
   184	        }
   185	    }
   186	#endif
   187	
   188	  /* Then enter the command line parsing loop */
   189	
   190	  for (; ; )
   191	    {
   192	      /* For the case of debugging the USB console...
   193	       * dump collected USB trace data
   194	       */
   195	
   196	#ifdef CONFIG_NSH_USBDEV_TRACE
   197	      nsh_usbtrace();
   198	#endif
   199	
   200	      /* Get the next line of input. readline() returns EOF
   201	       * on end-of-file or any read failure.
   202	       */
   203	
   204	#ifdef CONFIG_NSH_CLE
   205	      /* cle() normally returns the number of characters read, but will
   206	       * return a negated errno value on end of file or if an error
   207	       * occurs. Either  will cause the session to terminate.
   208	       */
   209	
   210	      ret = cle_fd(pstate->cn_line, nsh_prompt(), CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN,
   211	                   INFD(pstate), OUTFD(pstate));
   212	      if (ret == EOF)
   213	        {
   214	          dprintf(ERRFD(pstate), g_fmtcmdfailed, "nsh_session",
   215	                  "cle", NSH_ERRNO_OF(-ret));
   216	          ret = EXIT_SUCCESS;
   217	          break;
   218	        }
   219	#else
   220	      /* Display the prompt string */
   221	
   222	      write(OUTFD(pstate), nsh_prompt(), strlen(nsh_prompt()));
   223	
   224	      /* readline() normally returns the number of characters read, but
   225	       * will return EOF on end of file or if an error occurs.  EOF
   226	       * will cause the session to terminate.
   227	       */
   228	
   229	      ret = readline_fd(pstate->cn_line, CONFIG_NSH_LINELEN,
   230	                        INFD(pstate), OUTFD(pstate));
   231	      if (ret == EOF)
   232	        {
   233	          /* NOTE: readline() does not set the errno variable, but
   234	           * perhaps we will be lucky and it will still be valid.
   235	           */
   236	
   237	          dprintf(ERRFD(pstate), g_fmtcmdfailed, "nsh_session",
   238	                  "readline", NSH_ERRNO);
   239	          ret = EXIT_SUCCESS;
   240	          break;
   241	        }
   242	#endif
   243	
   244	      /* Parse process the command */
   245	
   246	      nsh_parse(vtbl, pstate->cn_line);
   247	      nsh_update_prompt();
   248	    }
   249	
   250	  return ret;
   251	}

    52	/****************************************************************************
    53	 * Name: nxtask_spawn_create
    54	 *
    55	 * Description:
    56	 *   This function creates and activates a new thread of the specified type
    57	 *   with a specified priority and returns its system-assigned ID.  It is the
    58	 *   internal, common implementation of task_create() and kthread_create().
    59	 *   See comments with task_create() for further information.
    60	 *
    61	 * Input Parameters:
    62	 *   name       - Name of the new task
    63	 *   entry      - Entry point of a new task
    64	 *   actions    - The spawn file actions
    65	 *   attr       - Use attr set stacksize, stackaddr and priority.
    66	 *   arg        - A pointer to an array of input parameters.  The array
    67	 *                should be terminated with a NULL argv[] value. If no
    68	 *                parameters are required, argv may be NULL.
    69	 *   envp       - A pointer to an array of environment strings. Terminated
    70	 *                with a NULL entry.
    71	 *
    72	 * Returned Value:
    73	 *   Returns the positive, non-zero process ID of the new task or a negated
    74	 *   errno value to indicate the nature of any failure.  If memory is
    75	 *   insufficient or the task cannot be created -ENOMEM will be returned.
    76	 *
    77	 ****************************************************************************/
    78	
    79	static int nxtask_spawn_create(FAR const char *name, main_t entry,
    80	                               FAR const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions,
    81	                               FAR const posix_spawnattr_t *attr,
    82	                               FAR char * const argv[],
    83	                               FAR char * const envp[])
    84	{
    85	  FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
    86	  pid_t pid;
    87	  int ret;
    88	
    89	  DEBUGASSERT(attr);
    90	
    91	  /* Allocate a TCB for the new task. */
    92	
    93	  tcb = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct tcb_s) + sizeof(struct task_group_s));
    94	  if (tcb == NULL)
    95	    {
    96	      serr("ERROR: Failed to allocate TCB\n");
    97	      ret = -ENOMEM;
    98	    }
    99	  else
   100	    {
   101	      /* Setup the task type */
   102	
   103	      atomic_set(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_TASK | TCB_FLAG_FREE_TCB);
   104	
   105	      /* Initialize the task */
   106	
   107	      ret = nxtask_init(tcb, name, entry, actions, attr, argv, envp);
   108	      if (ret < OK)
   109	        {
   110	          kmm_free(tcb);
   111	        }
   112	      else
   113	        {
   114	          /* Get the assigned pid before we start the task */
   115	
   116	          pid = tcb->pid;
   117	
   118	          /* Set the attributes */
   119	
   120	          ret = spawn_execattrs(pid, attr);
   121	          if (ret < 0)
   122	            {
   123	              nxtask_uninit(tcb);
   124	            }
   125	          else
   126	            {
   127	              /* Activate the task */
   128	
   129	              nxtask_activate(tcb);
   130	
   131	              ret = pid;
   132	            }
   133	        }
   134	    }
   135	
   136	  return ret;
   137	}

   139	/****************************************************************************
   140	 * Name: nxtask_spawn_exec
   141	 *
   142	 * Description:
   143	 *   Execute the task from the file system.
   144	 *
   145	 * Input Parameters:
   146	 *
   147	 *   pidp - Upon successful completion, this will return the task ID of the
   148	 *     child task in the variable pointed to by a non-NULL 'pid' argument.|
   149	 *
   150	 *   name - The name to assign to the child task.
   151	 *
   152	 *   entry - The child task's entry point (an address in memory)
   153	 *
   154	 *   actions - The spawn file actions
   155	 *
   156	 *   attr - If the value of the 'attr' parameter is NULL, the all default
   157	 *     values for the POSIX spawn attributes will be used.  Otherwise, the
   158	 *     attributes will be set according to the spawn flags.  The
   159	 *     following spawn flags are supported:
   160	 *
   161	 *     - POSIX_SPAWN_SETSCHEDPARAM: Set new tasks priority to the sched_param
   162	 *       value.
   163	 *     - POSIX_SPAWN_SETSCHEDULER: Set the new tasks scheduler priority to
   164	 *       the sched_policy value.
   165	 *
   166	 *     NOTE: POSIX_SPAWN_SETSIGMASK is handled in nxtask_spawn_proxy().
   167	 *
   168	 *   argv - argv[] is the argument list for the new task.  argv[] is an
   169	 *     array of pointers to null-terminated strings. The list is terminated
   170	 *     with a null pointer.
   171	 *
   172	 *   envp - A pointer to an array of environment strings. Terminated with
   173	 *     a NULL entry.
   174	 *
   175	 * Returned Value:
   176	 *   This function will return zero on success. Otherwise, an error number
   177	 *   will be returned as the function return value to indicate the error.
   178	 *   This errno value may be that set by execv(), sched_setpolicy(), or
   179	 *   sched_setparam().
   180	 *
   181	 ****************************************************************************/
   182	
   183	static int nxtask_spawn_exec(FAR pid_t *pidp, FAR const char *name,
   184	                             main_t entry,
   185	                             FAR const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions,
   186	                             FAR const posix_spawnattr_t *attr,
   187	                             FAR char * const *argv, FAR char * const envp[])
   188	{
   189	  posix_spawnattr_t tmp;
   190	  int pid;
   191	  int ret = OK;
   192	
   193	  /* Use the default priority and stack size if no attributes are provided */
   194	
   195	  if (!attr)
   196	    {
   197	      struct sched_param param;
   198	
   199	      /* Set the default priority to the same priority as this task */
   200	
   201	      ret = nxsched_get_param(0, &param);
   202	      if (ret == OK)
   203	        {
   204	          posix_spawnattr_init(&tmp);
   205	          posix_spawnattr_setschedparam(&tmp, &param);
   206	          posix_spawnattr_setstacksize(&tmp,
   207	                                       CONFIG_POSIX_SPAWN_DEFAULT_STACKSIZE);
   208	          attr = &tmp;
   209	        }
   210	    }
   211	
   212	  if (ret == OK)
   213	    {
   214	      /* Start the task */
   215	
   216	      pid = nxtask_spawn_create(name, entry, actions, attr, argv,
   217	                                envp ? envp : environ);
   218	
   219	      if (attr == &tmp)
   220	        {
   221	          posix_spawnattr_destroy(&tmp);
   222	        }
   223	
   224	      if (pid < 0)
   225	        {
   226	          ret = pid;
   227	          serr("ERROR: nxtask_spawn_create failed: %d\n", ret);
   228	        }
   229	
   230	      /* Return the task ID to the caller */
   231	
   232	      else if (pid)
   233	        {
   234	          *pidp = pid;
   235	        }
   236	    }
   237	
   238	  return ret;
   239	}

    43	/****************************************************************************
    44	 * Name: up_initial_state
    45	 *
    46	 * Description:
    47	 *   A new thread is being started and a new TCB
    48	 *   has been created. This function is called to initialize
    49	 *   the processor specific portions of the new TCB.
    50	 *
    51	 *   This function must setup the initial architecture registers
    52	 *   and/or  stack so that execution will begin at tcb->start
    53	 *   on the next context switch.
    54	 *
    55	 ****************************************************************************/
    56	
    57	void up_initial_state(struct tcb_s *tcb)
    58	{
    59	  struct xcptcontext *xcp = &tcb->xcp;
    60	#if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_RV_ISA_V) && (CONFIG_ARCH_RV_VECTOR_BYTE_LENGTH == 0)
    61	  uintptr_t *vregs = tcb->vregs;
    62	#endif
    63	  uintptr_t regval;
    64	  uintptr_t topstack;
    65	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK
    66	  uintptr_t *kstack = xcp->kstack;
    67	#endif
    68	
    69	  /* Initialize the initial exception register context structure */
    70	
    71	  memset(xcp, 0, sizeof(struct xcptcontext));
    72	
    73	#if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_RV_ISA_V) && (CONFIG_ARCH_RV_VECTOR_BYTE_LENGTH == 0)
    74	
    75	  /* Initialize vector registers */
    76	
    77	  if (vregs == NULL)
    78	    {
    79	      regval = READ_CSR(CSR_VLENB);
    80	      if (regval != 0)
    81	        {
    82	          /* There are 32 vector registers(v0 - v31) with vlenb length. */
    83	
    84	          xcp->vregs = kmm_calloc(1, regval * 32 + VPU_XCPT_SIZE);
    85	          DEBUGASSERT(xcp->vregs != NULL);
    86	        }
    87	    }
    88	  else
    89	    {
    90	      /* Keep the vector region if task restart */
    91	
    92	      xcp->vregs = vregs;
    93	    }
    94	#endif
    95	
    96	  /* Initialize the idle thread stack */
    97	
    98	  if (tcb->pid == IDLE_PROCESS_ID)
    99	    {
   100	      tcb->stack_alloc_ptr = (void *)g_cpux_idlestack(this_cpu());
   101	      tcb->stack_base_ptr  = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
   102	      tcb->adj_stack_size  = SMP_IDLE_STACK_SIZE;
   103	
   104	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK
   105	      /* Setup shadow stack for idle task */
   106	
   107	      xcp->sstack_alloc_ptr =
   108	        (uintreg_t *)g_cpux_idleshadowstack(this_cpu());
   109	      xcp->sstack_top_ptr = (uintreg_t *)((uintptr_t)xcp->sstack_alloc_ptr +
   110	                                          SMP_SHADOW_STACK_SIZE);
   111	#endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK */
   112	
   113	#ifdef CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION
   114	      /* If stack debug is enabled, then fill the stack with a
   115	       * recognizable value that we can use later to test for high
   116	       * water marks.
   117	       */
   118	
   119	      riscv_stack_color(tcb->stack_alloc_ptr, 0);
   120	#endif /* CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION */
   121	
   122	      /* Set idle process' initial interrupt context */
   123	
   124	      riscv_set_idleintctx();
   125	      return;
   126	    }
   127	
   128	  topstack = (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size;
   129	
   130	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK
   131	  /* Use the process kernel stack to store context for user processes */
   132	
   133	  if (kstack)
   134	    {
   135	      xcp->kstack  = kstack;
   136	      xcp->ustkptr = (uintptr_t *)topstack;
   137	      topstack     = (uintptr_t)kstack + ARCH_KERNEL_STACKSIZE;
   138	      xcp->ktopstk = (uintptr_t *)topstack;
   139	      xcp->kstkptr = xcp->ktopstk;
   140	    }
   141	#endif
   142	
   143	  xcp->regs = (uintreg_t *)(topstack - XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
   144	  memset(xcp->regs, 0, XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
   145	
   146	  /* Save the initial stack pointer.  Hmmm.. the stack is set to the very
   147	   * beginning of the stack region.  Some functions may want to store data on
   148	   * the caller's stack and it might be good to reserve some space.  However,
   149	   * only the start function would do that and we have control over that one
   150	   */
   151	
   152	  xcp->regs[REG_SP]      = topstack;
   153	
   154	  /* Save the task entry point */
   155	
   156	  xcp->regs[REG_EPC]     = (uintptr_t)tcb->start;
   157	
   158	  /* Setup thread local storage pointer */
   159	
   160	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_THREAD_LOCAL
   161	  xcp->regs[REG_TP]      = (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr +
   162	                                     sizeof(struct tls_info_s);
   163	#endif
   164	
   165	  /* Set the initial value of the interrupt context register.
   166	   *
   167	   * Since various RISC-V platforms use different interrupt
   168	   * methodologies, the value of the interrupt context is
   169	   * part specific.
   170	   *
   171	   */
   172	
   173	  regval = riscv_get_newintctx();
   174	  xcp->regs[REG_INT_CTX] = regval;
   175	
   176	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK
   177	  xcp->regs[REG_SSP] = (uintreg_t)xcp->sstack_top_ptr;
   178	#endif
   179	
   180	  /* Initialize the state of the extended context */
   181	
   182	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RISCV_INTXCPT_EXTENSIONS
   183	  riscv_initial_extctx_state(tcb);
   184	#endif
   185	
   186	#ifndef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
   187	  tcb->xcp.initregs = tcb->xcp.regs;

   173	 * Name:  sched_unlock
   174	 *
   175	 * Description:
   176	 *   This function decrements the preemption lock count.  Typically this
   177	 *   is paired with sched_lock() and concludes a critical section of
   178	 *   code.  Preemption will not be unlocked until sched_unlock() has
   179	 *   been called as many times as sched_lock().  When the lockcount is
   180	 *   decremented to zero, any tasks that were eligible to preempt the
   181	 *   current task will execute.
   182	 *
   183	 ****************************************************************************/

   185	#undef sched_unlock
   186	void sched_unlock(void)
   187	{
   188	  /* sched_unlock should have no effect if called from the interrupt level. */
   189	
   190	  FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
   191	
   192	  /* rtcb may be NULL only during early boot-up phases */
   193	
   194	  DEBUGASSERT(rtcb && rtcb->lockcount > 0);
   195	
   196	  /* Check if the lock counter has decremented to zero. If so,
   197	   * then pre-emption has been re-enabled.
   198	   */
   199	
   200	  if (rtcb->lockcount == 1)
   201	    {
   202	      nxsched_unlock(rtcb);
   203	    }

   134	void ESP_TIMER_IRAM_ATTR esp_timer_impl_set_alarm_id(uint64_t timestamp, unsigned alarm_id)

   136	    assert(alarm_id < sizeof(timestamp_id) / sizeof(timestamp_id[0]));
   137	    esp_os_enter_critical_safe(&s_time_update_lock);
   138	    timestamp_id[alarm_id] = timestamp;
   139	    timestamp = MIN(timestamp_id[0], timestamp_id[1]);
   140	    if (timestamp != UINT64_MAX) {
   141	        int64_t offset = LACT_TICKS_PER_US * 2;
   142	        uint64_t now_time = esp_timer_impl_get_counter_reg();
   143	        timer_64b_reg_t alarm = { .val = MAX(timestamp * LACT_TICKS_PER_US, now_time + offset) };
   144	        do {
   145	            REG_CLR_BIT(CONFIG_REG, TIMG_LACT_ALARM_EN);
   146	            REG_WRITE(ALARM_LO_REG, alarm.lo);
   147	            REG_WRITE(ALARM_HI_REG, alarm.hi);
   148	            REG_SET_BIT(CONFIG_REG, TIMG_LACT_ALARM_EN);
   149	            now_time = esp_timer_impl_get_counter_reg();
   150	            int64_t delta = (int64_t)alarm.val - (int64_t)now_time;

   153	                offset += llabs(delta) + LACT_TICKS_PER_US * 2;

   156	                // finish if either (alarm > counter) or the interrupt flag is already set.
   157	                break;
   158	            }
   159	        } while (1);

   164	static void ESP_TIMER_IRAM_ATTR timer_alarm_isr(void *arg)
   165	{
   166	#if ISR_HANDLERS == 1
   167	    /* Clear interrupt status */
   168	    REG_WRITE(INT_CLR_REG, TIMG_LACT_INT_CLR);
   169	
   170	    /* Call the upper layer handler */
   171	    (*s_alarm_handler)(arg);
   172	#else
   173	    static volatile uint32_t processed_by = NOT_USED;
   174	    static volatile bool pending_alarm = false;
   175	    /* CRITICAL section ensures the read/clear is atomic between cores */
   176	    esp_os_enter_critical_isr(&s_time_update_lock);
   177	    if (REG_GET_FIELD(INT_ST_REG, TIMG_LACT_INT_ST)) {
   178	        // Clear interrupt status
   179	        REG_WRITE(INT_CLR_REG, TIMG_LACT_INT_CLR);
   180	        // Is the other core already processing a previous alarm?
   181	        if (processed_by == NOT_USED) {
   182	            // Current core is not processing an alarm yet
   183	            processed_by = OS_PORT_GET_CORE_ID();
   184	            do {
   185	                pending_alarm = false;
   186	                // Clear interrupt status
   187	                REG_WRITE(INT_CLR_REG, TIMG_LACT_INT_CLR);
   188	                esp_os_exit_critical_isr(&s_time_update_lock);
   189	
   190	                (*s_alarm_handler)(arg);
   191	
   192	                esp_os_enter_critical_isr(&s_time_update_lock);
   193	                // Another alarm could have occurred while were handling the previous alarm.
   194	                // Check if we need to call the s_alarm_handler again:
   195	                //   1) if the alarm has already been fired, it helps to handle it immediately without an additional ISR call.
   196	                //   2) handle pending alarm that was cleared by the other core in time when this core worked with the current alarm.
   197	            } while (REG_GET_FIELD(INT_ST_REG, TIMG_LACT_INT_ST) || pending_alarm);
   198	            processed_by = NOT_USED;
   199	        } else {
   200	            // Current core arrived at ISR but the other core is still handling a previous alarm.
   201	            // Once we already cleared the ISR status we need to let the other core know that it was.
   202	            // Set the flag to handle the current alarm by the other core later.
   203	            pending_alarm = true;
   204	        }
   205	    }
   206	    esp_os_exit_critical_isr(&s_time_update_lock);
   207	#endif // ISR_HANDLERS != 1

    82	    {
    83	      /* Set up default signal actions for NON-kernel thread */
    84	
    85	      nxsig_default_initialize(tcb);
    86	    }
    87	#endif
    88	
    89	  /* Take args from stack, as group is shared for kthreads */
    90	
    91	  argv = nxsched_get_stackargs(tcb);
    92	  for (argc = 0; argv && argv[argc]; argc++);
    93	
    94	  /* Call the 'main' entry point passing argc and argv.  In the kernel build
    95	   * this has to be handled differently if we are starting a user-space task;
    96	   * we have to switch to user-mode before calling the task.
    97	   */
    98	
    99	  if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL)
   100	    {
   101	      exitcode = entry_main(argc, argv);
   102	    }
   103	  else
   104	    {
   105	#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
   106	      up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
   107	      nxtask_startup(entry_main, argc, argv);
   108	#else
   109	      up_task_start(entry_main, argc, argv);
   110	#endif
   111	    }

    45	 *
    46	 * Description:
    47	 *   A new thread is being started and a new TCB
    48	 *   has been created. This function is called to initialize
    49	 *   the processor specific portions of the new TCB.
    50	 *
    51	 *   This function must setup the initial architecture registers
    52	 *   and/or  stack so that execution will begin at tcb->start
    53	 *   on the next context switch.
    54	 *
    55	 ****************************************************************************/
    56	
    57	void up_initial_state(struct tcb_s *tcb)
    58	{
    59	  struct xcptcontext *xcp = &tcb->xcp;
    60	#if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_RV_ISA_V) && (CONFIG_ARCH_RV_VECTOR_BYTE_LENGTH == 0)
    61	  uintptr_t *vregs = tcb->vregs;
    62	#endif
    63	  uintptr_t regval;
    64	  uintptr_t topstack;
    65	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK
    66	  uintptr_t *kstack = xcp->kstack;
    67	#endif
    68	
    69	  /* Initialize the initial exception register context structure */
    70	
    71	  memset(xcp, 0, sizeof(struct xcptcontext));
    72	
    73	#if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_RV_ISA_V) && (CONFIG_ARCH_RV_VECTOR_BYTE_LENGTH == 0)
    74	
    75	  /* Initialize vector registers */
    76	
    77	  if (vregs == NULL)
    78	    {
    79	      regval = READ_CSR(CSR_VLENB);
    80	      if (regval != 0)
    81	        {
    82	          /* There are 32 vector registers(v0 - v31) with vlenb length. */
    83	
    84	          xcp->vregs = kmm_calloc(1, regval * 32 + VPU_XCPT_SIZE);
    85	          DEBUGASSERT(xcp->vregs != NULL);
    86	        }
    87	    }
    88	  else
    89	    {
    90	      /* Keep the vector region if task restart */
    91	
    92	      xcp->vregs = vregs;
    93	    }
    94	#endif
    95	
    96	  /* Initialize the idle thread stack */
    97	
    98	  if (tcb->pid == IDLE_PROCESS_ID)
    99	    {
   100	      tcb->stack_alloc_ptr = (void *)g_cpux_idlestack(this_cpu());
   101	      tcb->stack_base_ptr  = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
   102	      tcb->adj_stack_size  = SMP_IDLE_STACK_SIZE;
   103	
   104	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK
   105	      /* Setup shadow stack for idle task */
   106	
   107	      xcp->sstack_alloc_ptr =
   108	        (uintreg_t *)g_cpux_idleshadowstack(this_cpu());
   109	      xcp->sstack_top_ptr = (uintreg_t *)((uintptr_t)xcp->sstack_alloc_ptr +
   110	                                          SMP_SHADOW_STACK_SIZE);
   111	#endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK */
   112	
   113	#ifdef CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION
   114	      /* If stack debug is enabled, then fill the stack with a
   115	       * recognizable value that we can use later to test for high
   116	       * water marks.
   117	       */
   118	
   119	      riscv_stack_color(tcb->stack_alloc_ptr, 0);
   120	#endif /* CONFIG_STACK_COLORATION */
   121	
   122	      /* Set idle process' initial interrupt context */
   123	
   124	      riscv_set_idleintctx();
   125	      return;
   126	    }
   127	
   128	  topstack = (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_base_ptr + tcb->adj_stack_size;
   129	
   130	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK
   131	  /* Use the process kernel stack to store context for user processes */
   132	
   133	  if (kstack)
   134	    {
   135	      xcp->kstack  = kstack;
   136	      xcp->ustkptr = (uintptr_t *)topstack;
   137	      topstack     = (uintptr_t)kstack + ARCH_KERNEL_STACKSIZE;
   138	      xcp->ktopstk = (uintptr_t *)topstack;
   139	      xcp->kstkptr = xcp->ktopstk;
   140	    }
   141	#endif
   142	
   143	  xcp->regs = (uintreg_t *)(topstack - XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
   144	  memset(xcp->regs, 0, XCPTCONTEXT_SIZE);
   145	
   146	  /* Save the initial stack pointer.  Hmmm.. the stack is set to the very
   147	   * beginning of the stack region.  Some functions may want to store data on
   148	   * the caller's stack and it might be good to reserve some space.  However,
   149	   * only the start function would do that and we have control over that one
   150	   */
   151	
   152	  xcp->regs[REG_SP]      = topstack;
   153	
   154	  /* Save the task entry point */
   155	
   156	  xcp->regs[REG_EPC]     = (uintptr_t)tcb->start;
   157	
   158	  /* Setup thread local storage pointer */
   159	
   160	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_THREAD_LOCAL
   161	  xcp->regs[REG_TP]      = (uintptr_t)tcb->stack_alloc_ptr +
   162	                                     sizeof(struct tls_info_s);
   163	#endif
   164	
   165	  /* Set the initial value of the interrupt context register.
   166	   *
   167	   * Since various RISC-V platforms use different interrupt
   168	   * methodologies, the value of the interrupt context is
   169	   * part specific.
   170	   *
   171	   */
   172	
   173	  regval = riscv_get_newintctx();
   174	  xcp->regs[REG_INT_CTX] = regval;
   175	
   176	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RV_SHADOW_STACK
   177	  xcp->regs[REG_SSP] = (uintreg_t)xcp->sstack_top_ptr;
   178	#endif
   179	
   180	  /* Initialize the state of the extended context */
   181	
   182	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_RISCV_INTXCPT_EXTENSIONS
   183	  riscv_initial_extctx_state(tcb);
   184	#endif
   185	
   186	#ifndef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
   187	  tcb->xcp.initregs = tcb->xcp.regs;
   188	#endif
   189	}

   423	   */

   427	#if defined(CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL) || \

   430	  uint32_t rx_thrs = 0;

   432	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_IFLOWCONTROL
   433	  /* Configure the input flow control */
   434	
   435	  if (priv->iflow)
   436	    {
   437	      /* Enable input flow control and set the RX FIFO threshold
   438	       * to assert the RTS line to half the RX FIFO buffer.
   439	       * It will then save some space on the hardware fifo to

   441	       * and before the transmitter stops sending data.
   442	       */
   443	
   444	      flow_ctrl |= UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_RTS;
   445	      rx_thrs = SOC_UART_FIFO_LEN / 2;

   448	
   449	#ifdef CONFIG_SERIAL_OFLOWCONTROL
   450	  /* Configure the output flow control */
   451	
   452	  if (priv->oflow)

   454	      flow_ctrl |= UART_HW_FLOWCTRL_CTS;

   577	/****************************************************************************
   578	 * Name: esp_txint
   579	 *
   580	 * Description:
   581	 *   Enable or disable TX interrupts.
   582	 *

   584	 *   dev           - Pointer to the serial driver struct.
   585	 *   enable        - If true enables the TX interrupt, if false disables it.
   586	 *
   587	 * Returned Value:
   588	 *   None.
   589	 *
   590	 ****************************************************************************/
   591	
   592	static void esp_txint(uart_dev_t *dev, bool enable)
